cat > 'pod.yaml' <<'KUBEQUEST_FILE'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:

  labels:

  namespace: mynamespace

      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

core-concepts-30a3e4723da4.title: Read a container’s environment
core-concepts-30a3e4723da4.tagline: A short-lived container can reveal its environment without a long-running service.
core-concepts-30a3e4723da4.solution:
cat > 'env.yaml' <<'KUBEQUEST_FILE'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: env-reader
  labels:
    run: env-reader
spec:
  containers:
    - name: env-reader
      image: busybox:1.37
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      command:
        - env
  restartPolicy: Never
KUBEQUEST_FILE
kubectl apply -f env.yaml
kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded pod/env-reader --timeout=90s
kubectl logs env-reader > answer.txt
cat answer.txt

checks.label: The env process completed
checks.command: kubectl get pod/env-reader -n quest -o json | jq -e '.status.phase == "Succeeded" and .spec.restartPolicy == "Never"' >/dev/null

checks.label: The saved evidence contains the requested result
checks.command:
test -s answer.txt
grep -F -- 'HOSTNAME=env-reader' answer.txt >/dev/null

core-concepts-30a3e4723da4.why: The env process prints its environment and exits. restartPolicy Never preserves completion instead of repeatedly restarting a successful one-shot command.
core-concepts-30a3e4723da4.brief: Run a busybox:1.37 Pod named env-reader with command env and restartPolicy Never. Save its logs to answer.txt.

core-concepts-f44e364f1cfd.title: Reach a Pod by IP
core-concepts-f44e364f1cfd.tagline: Test the server from another Pod.
core-concepts-f44e364f1cfd.setup:
kubectl apply -f - <<'KUBEQUEST_YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    run: nginx
spec:
  containers:
    - name: nginx
      image: nginx:1.28
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
KUBEQUEST_YAML

grep -F -- 'Welcome to nginx' answer.txt >/dev/null

core-concepts-f44e364f1cfd.why: A Pod IP routes directly to that Pod while it exists. A successful HTTP response tests more than merely observing an assigned address.

core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.title: Recover the previous logs
core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.tagline: A restart should not erase the first clue.
core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.setup:
kubectl apply -f - <<'KUBEQUEST_YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: logger
  labels:
    run: logger
spec:
  containers:
    - name: logger
      image: busybox:1.37
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - echo KUBEQUEST_PREVIOUS_INSTANCE; if [ -f /state/restarted ]; then
          sleep 3600; else touch /state/restarted; sleep 10; exit 1; fi
      volumeMounts:
        - name: state
          mountPath: /state
  volumes:
    - name: state
      emptyDir: {}
KUBEQUEST_YAML
for i in $(seq 1 60); do test "$(kubectl get pod logger -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}')" -ge 1 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 2; done
kubectl wait -n quest --for=condition=Ready pod/logger --timeout=90s
core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.solution:
kubectl logs logger --previous > answer.txt
cat answer.txt

checks.label: The saved evidence contains the requested result
checks.command:
test -s answer.txt
grep -F -- 'KUBEQUEST_PREVIOUS_INSTANCE' answer.txt >/dev/null

core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.why: --previous requests the preceding terminated container instance. It is especially useful when a restart has replaced the process whose failure you need to investigate.
core-concepts-6c4359ff0c03.brief: The logger Pod has restarted. Save the previous container instance’s logs to answer.txt using --previous.

core-concepts-c7716ab3c79b.title: Finish a one-shot Pod

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hello
  labels:
    run: hello
spec:
  containers:
    - name: hello
      image: busybox:1.37
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      command:
        - echo
        - hello world

core-concepts-c7716ab3c79b.why: Never leaves a successful one-shot container completed; the output remains available until the Pod is deleted.
core-concepts-c7716ab3c79b.brief: Create Pod hello that prints hello world and exits successfully. Save the logs to answer.txt.

core-concepts-314d16e6bd4e.title: Inject a container variable

multi-container-pods-b17c25b2c8e7.title: Choose the right container
multi-container-pods-b17c25b2c8e7.tagline: Two containers share a Pod, but exec needs a destination.
multi-container-pods-b17c25b2c8e7.solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'KUBEQUEST_YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: double
  labels:
    run: double
spec:
  containers:
    - name: first
      image: busybox:1.37
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      command: &a1
        - sh
        - -c
        - echo hello; sleep 3600
    - name: second
      image: busybox:1.37

pod-design-326c7efa4cb4.title: Keep the scheduled output
pod-design-326c7efa4cb4.tagline: Capture the result before cleaning up.

startup-probe-budget.title: Give a slow application time to start
startup-probe-budget.tagline: Protect initialization, then prove steady-state recovery.
startup-probe-budget.setup:
kubectl create namespace kq-startup
cat > 'slow.yaml' <<'KUBEQUEST_FILE'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow
  namespace: kq-startup
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37
      command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - sleep 25; touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 3600
      startupProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
        failureThreshold: 30
      livenessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 5
        failureThreshold: 3
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
KUBEQUEST_FILE
kubectl apply -f slow.yaml
kubectl wait -n kq-startup --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=90s
startup-probe-budget.solution:
cat > 'slow.yaml' <<'KUBEQUEST_FILE'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow
  namespace: kq-startup
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37
      command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - sleep 45; touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 3600
      startupProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
        failureThreshold: 45
      livenessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 5
        failureThreshold: 3
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
KUBEQUEST_FILE
kubectl delete pod slow -n kq-startup
kubectl apply -f slow.yaml
kubectl wait -n kq-startup --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=90s
kubectl exec -n kq-startup slow -- rm /tmp/healthy
for i in $(seq 1 60); do test "$(kubectl get pod slow -n kq-startup -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}')" -ge 1 && break; sleep 2; done
kubectl wait -n kq-startup --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=90s

checks.label: The startup budget is configured
checks.command: kubectl get pod/slow -n kq-startup -o json | jq -e '.spec.containers[0].startupProbe | .failureThreshold == 45 and .periodSeconds == 2' >/dev/null

checks.label: The liveness check remains intact
checks.command: kubectl get pod/slow -n kq-startup -o json | jq -e '.spec.containers[0].livenessProbe | .periodSeconds == 5 and .failureThreshold == 3' >/dev/null

startup-probe-budget.why: Until a startup probe succeeds, Kubernetes holds back liveness and readiness probes. After startup succeeds, liveness detects a broken process and readiness controls traffic eligibility. The startup failureThreshold × periodSeconds gives an approximate failure budget, not an exact stopwatch.
startup-probe-budget.brief: Change the startup delay to 45 seconds and allow approximately 90 seconds for startup. Keep the existing two-second startup period and steady-state liveness settings. Recreate the Pod, confirm successful startup, then remove the healthy file to prove liveness still restarts the container.
